entries.what_happened: Four manuscripts are in the family; the first is the direct match and the others bear on it only through Seshadri forms. (a) 'Nagata's conjecture for plane curves' (folder Nagatas-Conjecture-for-Plane-Curves-September-23-2026, dated 23 September 2026). Theorem 1.1 (thm:main) claims that for every integer r ≥ 10 there is a countable union E_r of proper Zariski-closed subsets of U_r, the space of ordered r-tuples of distinct points of ℙ²_ℂ, with nonempty complement, such that for every tuple outside E_r, every nonzero effective plane curve of degree d ≥ 1 and all nonnegative integers m_i with multiplicity at p_i at least m_i satisfies d√r > Σm_i. Reducible and nonreduced curves are included, and the multiplicities need not be equal. Corollary cor:sesha (consequences section) reads this on the blow-up: √r·H − ΣE_i is strictly nef with self-intersection zero, so the multipoint Seshadri constant of O(1) is exactly 1/√r. The same corollary proves the matching upper bound by counting: forms of degree ⌈√r(n+1)⌉ with multiplicity n at all r points exist. Corollary cor:fields extends the statement to every uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, again with nonempty complement. (b) 'Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces' (23 September 2026) does not treat plane curves as such. Read as a specialization to S = ℙ² with L = O(1) (so L² = 1), its main theorem gives ε = 1/√r at very general tuples for every sufficiently large r, with no threshold computed. That specialization is my reading; the manuscript does not state it. (c) 'Maximal multipoint Seshadri constants in positive characteristic' (5 October 2026). Its dimension-two remark (rem:surfaces) asserts the same equality for ℙ² at the geometric generic tuple over any algebraically closed field of characteristic p, for r at or above a threshold. (d) 'Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions' (5 October 2026) treats dimension n ≥ 3 only and does not bear on plane curves.
entries.delivers: If the claim holds, it delivers the strict inequality of problem_asks (1) in full: for r ≥ 10 (the list's r > 9), at very general tuples over ℂ, every plane curve with multiplicities m_i at those points satisfies d > (1/√r)Σm_i. The manuscript says it establishes 'Nagata's conjecture in its strict, nonhomogeneous form', and its theorem covers every r ≥ 10, including the non-square r the list treats as open and the square r ≥ 16 that Nagata proved earlier. The part the list calls open is the degree lower bound, and that is the part claimed. The matching existence of curves is covered only by the counting upper bound in cor:sesha, which gives curves whose ratio tends to 1/√r. Field scope: the main theorem is over ℂ, and cor:fields extends it to uncountable algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero. The list allows only positive multiplicities; the manuscript allows zero, which is a weaker-looking but equivalent statement for this purpose. Read as the specialization in (b), the surfaces manuscript gives the Seshadri form only for sufficiently large r with no threshold, so it covers less than the Nagata paper does.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, nothing in problem_asks (1) remains open over ℂ or over uncountable algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero, at very general tuples. Not covered: (i) tuples that are not very general. The exceptional set E_r is a countable union of proper closed subsets, chosen simultaneously for all degrees and multiplicity vectors, and it is not given explicitly. (ii) Countable fields and positive characteristic, which the Nagata paper does not treat. The positive-characteristic paper gives the Seshadri form for large r only, at geometric generic tuples. (iii) Exact existence of curves attaining the bound for each degree. The manuscript proves only the asymptotic counting upper bound in cor:sesha.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture: the strict Nagata inequality for all r ≥ 10 at very general tuples over ℂ
entries.doubts: No step is flagged as sketched, conditional or omitted. A search of the proof sections for 'sketch', 'omit', 'routine', 'verify', 'assum' and similar terms found no such flags. Two points bear on trust. First, the key nonsquare step (contract a slice-width polygon, and absorb the integer endpoint error by passing to a common power of the curve) is stated in one paragraph of the introduction and worked out in Sections 02–04, which I did not read in full. Second, the proof uses theta-function product identities. The text says it proves these itself in the normalization it needs, citing Rosengren only for conventions.

entries.what_happened: The direct match is 'Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces' (23 September 2026). Its Theorem (thm:main) claims that for every smooth integral complex projective surface S and every ample line bundle L on S, there is an integer r_0(S,L) such that for each r ≥ r_0 there is a countable union Z_r of proper Zariski-closed subsets of U_r (ordered r-tuples of distinct points of S), with nonempty complement, such that for every tuple outside Z_r the class π*L − √(L²/r)·ΣE_i is nef on the blow-up. Hence ε(S,L; p_1,…,p_r) = √(L²/r) at those tuples. The universal bound ε ≤ √(L²/r) holds at every tuple and every r (Lemma sesha-upper, in nef.tex), so the content is the lower bound. Corollary cor:fields (nef.tex) extends the statement to smooth integral projective surfaces over any uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. The abstract calls this a positive resolution of the qualitative Nagata–Biran conjecture for surfaces. The introduction says that Harbourne (2003) already gave maximality for all sufficiently large r with rL² a square, for very ample L. The paper's own theorem covers all sufficiently large r, including the other values. The positive-characteristic paper's dimension-two remark (rem:surfaces) says the same conclusion holds for n = 2 at the geometric generic tuple over any algebraically closed field of characteristic p, for r at or above a threshold depending on (S,L). The higher-dimensional paper ('Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions', 5 October 2026) treats only dimension n ≥ 3, with value (L^n/r)^{1/n} at very general tuples, and does not address surfaces.
entries.delivers: If the claim holds, it establishes the qualitative Nagata–Biran statement for smooth integral complex projective surfaces. For each ample L there is an r_0 such that, for every r ≥ r_0, the Seshadri constant equals the stated value at very general r-tuples. The manuscript writes the value as √(L²/r), where L² is the self-intersection number. The list writes d/√r with d 'the degree' of L. The two agree only if d = √(L²), for example O(1) on ℙ², where L² = 1. The manuscript uses no letter d. The equality is exact for each large r, not merely asymptotic, and the upper bound holds at all tuples. The manuscript states that it resolves the conjecture positively for surfaces, and the list's 'sufficiently large r' regime matches r ≥ r_0. On scope, the list says 'a smooth algebraic surface' without qualification. The theorem covers smooth integral complex projective surfaces, and the corollary covers smooth integral projective surfaces over uncountable algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, the following remain. (i) Points: equality holds only off a countable union of proper closed subsets, that is, at very general tuples. The list's unqualified 'the points p_1,…,p_r' is not covered at arbitrary tuples, and the manuscript claims nothing for particular tuples. (ii) Surfaces: non-projective smooth algebraic surfaces, countable fields, and positive characteristic are not covered by this manuscript. The positive-characteristic paper's dimension-two remark covers characteristic p only at the geometric generic tuple, not at very general tuples. (iii) Threshold: r_0(S,L) is an existence statement that depends on the chosen nodal divisor and parameters. The manuscript gives no explicit bound and no uniformity over surfaces. (iv) The sharper threshold prediction of Strycharz-Szemberg–Szemberg, which the introduction cites as a stronger form of the conjecture, is not claimed.
entries.direction: proves maximality (Seshadri constant equal to the volume bound) for all sufficiently large r, at very general points, over ℂ and uncountable algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero
entries.doubts: The threshold r_0 is defined through the nodal divisor and lattice-direction choices made in the node, compression and lattice sections. Those sections carry the content, and I did not read them in full. A search of them found no sketch or omission flags. The introduction presents the construction for each sufficiently large r as tuned to a primitive lattice direction, with a torus subgroup of index r that need not be a square grid. The text does not say how large r_0 must be. The plane Nagata manuscript (OpenAINagata2026) is cited only in the introduction, as a separate refinement of the threshold and the strict inequality; I found no use of it in the proof sections. The introduction describes prior results (Harbourne 2003, and Roé's transfer, which assumes plane maximality) as context. It says the argument treats arbitrary polarizations directly rather than through them.
